scope: Service objectives, privacy-safe observability, performance budgets, and recovery verification design for a local-first desktop download manager. No application, production service, remote telemetry, or release-readiness claim exists.

dependencies.sharedRuleBoundary: The shared download domain and transfer service exclusively own state transitions, retry, resume, cancellation, destination, finalization, and recovery rules. UI, platform, storage, network, and telemetry adapters may observe facts but may not redefine those rules.

serviceObjectives.objective: Accepted commands receive a visible acknowledgement without transfer work blocking the UI thread.
serviceObjectives.candidateIndicator: p95 and p99 elapsed time from user command to rendered state acknowledgement
serviceObjectives.measurement: Instrument monotonic command-start, domain-acceptance, and rendered-state timestamps in a real desktop runtime under the approved workload.
serviceObjectives.status: candidate pending first-platform approval and runtime baseline

serviceObjectives.objective: Progress presentation remains responsive while transfers are active.
serviceObjectives.candidateIndicator: UI main-thread stall duration and input-to-render latency during representative concurrent downloads
serviceObjectives.measurement: Platform profiler plus scripted pause, resume, cancel, retry, and file-location interactions at each concurrency tier.
serviceObjectives.status: candidate; platform-specific thresholds must be approved

serviceObjectives.objective: Resource use is bounded and backpressure prevents concurrency from exhausting the device.
serviceObjectives.candidateIndicator: process CPU, resident memory, open handles, buffered bytes, disk queue depth, connections, and transfer concurrency
serviceObjectives.measurement: Soak and burst workloads on minimum and representative approved hardware; numerical ceilings are set from measured baselines, not invented here.
serviceObjectives.status: blocked pending platform, transfer implementation, and workload approval

serviceObjectives.objective: Restart recovery never presents an incomplete or unverified file as completed.
serviceObjectives.candidateIndicator: integrity-safe recovery outcomes divided by injected interruption scenarios
serviceObjectives.measurement: Terminate the process at deterministic persistence, write, and finalization fault points; restart and compare file hashes and durable state.

serviceObjectives.objective: Diagnostics operate locally without disclosing secrets or requiring a hosted service.
serviceObjectives.candidateIndicator: prohibited sensitive values found in structured logs and diagnostic exports
serviceObjectives.measurement: Seed unique canary values in URL user-info, query parameters, headers, cookies, credentials, destination paths, and filenames; scan every diagnostic sink and crash artifact.
serviceObjectives.status: mandatory privacy gate; executable evidence unavailable

telemetryPlan.default: Remote telemetry absent. Structured local diagnostics are enabled only at a minimal operational level and remain on-device.
cardinalityControls: ephemeral random session and download identifiers
telemetryPlan.retention: Local retention duration, size cap, export, and deletion UX require product/privacy approval; implementations must use finite defaults and user-initiated deletion.

performanceVerificationMatrix.environment: minimum and representative approved platform hardware

performanceVerificationMatrix.workload: approved maximum concurrent transfers across one and multiple hosts
performanceVerificationMatrix.environment: deterministic local HTTP servers plus shaped network

performanceVerificationMatrix.workload: rapid pause, resume, cancel, retry, and queue mutations during active transfers
large file and long soak with throttling and transient faults
performanceVerificationMatrix.environment: fault-injecting local server and temporary test destination

performanceVerificationMatrix.workload: slow disk and bounded write queue
performanceVerificationMatrix.environment: platform-appropriate disk shaping or controlled adapter

recoveryVerificationMatrix.expected: durable interrupted or failed state; no completed claim; retry follows shared policy; final hash must match source

recoveryVerificationMatrix.fault: process termination before metadata persistence, during body write, and during finalization
recoveryVerificationMatrix.expected: restart reconciliation is deterministic; partial remains distinguishable; false completion and silent corruption are zero
bounded failure result with actionable error code; existing destination is not damaged; retry requires restored capacity

recoveryVerificationMatrix.fault: server ignores Range or returns malformed Content-Range
recoveryVerificationMatrix.expected: resume is rejected and explicit restart policy is requested from the shared domain

recoveryVerificationMatrix.fault: remote identity or length changes between attempts
recoveryVerificationMatrix.expected: partial content is not appended; user-visible safe restart or failure path is selected by the shared domain

recoveryVerificationMatrix.fault: destination conflict, locked file, or final rename failure
recoveryVerificationMatrix.expected: original destination remains intact and completion is not recorded until approved conflict handling and finalization succeed

evidenceProtocol.comparison: Store candidate and baseline measurements using identical workload and environment profiles; report absolute values and percentage change. Do not average away platform-specific failures.
evidenceProtocol.failurePolicy: Any silent corruption, false completion, secret disclosure, unbounded growth, or missed mandatory invariant fails the candidate regardless of aggregate performance.

currentEvidence.reason: No executable application, approved first platform, approved workload, or numerical resource baseline exists in the repository.

alertingAndOperations.baseline: There is no hosted production service and therefore no paging or production alert channel.
alertingAndOperations.userCommunication: The UI adapter maps safe domain error codes to accessible status; logs are not a substitute for user-visible recovery guidance.
alertingAndOperations.futureHostedServices: If a release or telemetry service is approved later, define separate availability SLOs, burn-rate alerts, runbooks, ownership, and staging exercises before production approval.

traceability.limitation: Supported platform and hardware matrices remain unapproved.

implementationNotes: Instrumentation belongs at shared domain/service and adapter boundaries; UI and adapters must not duplicate or infer business state.
Use monotonic clocks for durations and wall-clock timestamps only for correlation.
Progress events must be coalesced or sampled so network chunk frequency cannot flood persistence, diagnostics, or the UI.
No user-visible behavior is implemented by this artifact, so DOM, browser, integration, or equivalent runtime testing is not applicable to this workstream.
Only local, test, and staging are declared; production activity requires separate attributed human approval.
knownRisks: The first platform, supported versions, MVP workload, UI foundation, and numerical resource ceilings remain unapproved.
Candidate latency values are planning targets, not measured commitments, and must be recalibrated on approved platform hardware.
No executable transfer, persistence, filesystem, or UI implementation exists, so performance and recovery outcomes are unverified.
Diagnostic retention and export behavior require a privacy decision before implementation.
Range and remote-identity mistakes can silently corrupt content unless the mandatory fault matrix is automated.
Independent verification remains outstanding and may only be issued by ENG-15.
